routes.name: Short stay in Estonia (Schengen)
routes.summary: Estonia is in Schengen. Short stays are up to 90 days in any 180 days, either visa-free or with a short-stay visa, depending on your passport.

other: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists these nationalities (plus EU, EEA and Schengen citizens) as not needing a visa for up to 90 days in any 180.
Anyone with a residence permit from a Schengen state also needs no visa.
Other nationalities need a Schengen short-stay visa. Airport transit visa rules were not confirmed.

sources.label: Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs: who does not need a visa
Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs: long-stay (D) visa page (mentions 90 days in 180 Schengen rule)

routes.name: Digital Nomad Visa (long-stay D visa for teleworking)
routes.summary: A visa of up to 365 days for people who work remotely for a foreign employer, a foreign company they own, or mostly foreign clients. It can't be extended and doesn't lead to a residence permit. e-Residency is a digital ID, not a visa, and isn't needed.

income.note: Ministry of Foreign Affairs says 132 EUR per day (3,960 per month). The e-Residency site says about 4,500 per month. Confirm before applying.

other: Must work location-independently using telecommunications.
One of: contract with a foreign-registered employer, owner or partner of a foreign-registered company, or freelance for mostly foreign clients.
Applications from Russian and Belarusian citizens are currently restricted.
Staying over 183 days in 12 months can make you an Estonian tax resident.
Income proof must cover the 3 months before you apply.

stay.note: Total stays capped at 548 days in 730 consecutive days. Also allows up to 90 days in other Schengen states per 180 days.

documents: Passport issued in last 10 years, valid 3 months past visa
Proof of remote work such as employer confirmation

routes.name: Start-up entrepreneur residence permit and start-up D visa
routes.summary: Founders of an evaluated start-up can get a business residence permit for up to 5 years. The company must be in the Estonian Business Register and pass an expert committee evaluation first. A short D visa for start-up business also exists.

income.note: This is the D visa funds requirement for start-up business (spouse 704). The residence permit needs income of four times the yearly subsistence level.

other: You must hold shares in an Estonian-registered company.
The start-up needs a positive evaluation from a Ministry of the Interior expert committee, or be exempt. The committee answers within 10 working days.
Health insurance required.
Register your address in Estonia after you get the permit.

sources.label: Police and Border Guard Board: residence permit for start-up entrepreneurs
Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs: long-stay D visa

stay.note: Permit up to 5 years, extensions up to 10 years at a time.

routes.processing: Decision within 90 days, then the card is issued within 30 days.

routes.name: Residence permit for employment (includes EU Blue Card)
routes.summary: For skilled and general employees with a job in Estonia. Salary generally must be at least the Estonian average gross salary. The employer first gets approval from the Unemployment Insurance Fund.

income.note: Gross, average salary rate for applications from 5 March 2026. Lower 1,674 and higher 2,594 and 3,138 rates apply to some categories.

other: Employer must be registered in Estonia and get permission from the Unemployment Insurance Fund.
Exceptions to the salary threshold exist.
After 5 years on an employment permit you need Estonian A2 to extend.

stay.note: Initial permit up to 5 years. Extensions up to 10 years at a time.

sources.label: Police and Border Guard Board: residence permit for employment

routes.processing: Decision within 90 days, then the card is issued within 30 days.

routes.name: Long-stay D visa for study, short-term work or seasonal work
routes.summary: The D visa covers studies, PhD studies, short-term work (including in a start-up) and seasonal work. Each has its own funds requirement.

other: Funds required: studies 880 EUR per month (spouse 2,100). PhD 880 per month (spouse 704).
Short-term employment 1,320 EUR once. Short-term work at a start-up or seasonal work 880 EUR once (spouse 704).
Proof of income for the 3 months before you apply.

sources.label: Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs: long-stay D visa

routes.name: Youth visa with work rights (working holiday style)
routes.summary: Under bilateral agreements, young citizens of Australia, New Zealand, Canada and Japan can get a long-stay visa with work rights.

other: Age limits and duration not confirmed. Check with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

sources.label: Estonian Ministry of Foreign Affairs: long-stay D visa

routes.name: Residence permit for a spouse (family member)
routes.summary: For a spouse of an Estonian citizen or of a foreigner living in Estonia on a residence permit. Similar family permits exist for children and parents.

other: Sponsor must be an Estonian citizen or a foreigner with an Estonian residence permit.
Sponsor must have income of double the subsistence level, set yearly by the State Budget Act.
Health insurance required.
No language requirement is mentioned on the page.
Spouses of employment or study permit holders qualify only in exceptional cases.

stay.note: Initial permit up to 5 years, and no longer than the sponsor's permit. Extensions up to 10 years at a time.

sources.label: Police and Border Guard Board: residence permit for a spouse

routes.name: Residence permit for a permanent resident (long-term resident)
routes.summary: For people who have lived in Estonia on a temporary permit and settled here. Needs 3 of the last 5 years and Estonian A2. You need it for citizenship.

eligibility.language: Estonian A2 (exam not needed if you were educated in Estonian)
other: Lived in Estonia at least 3 out of 5 consecutive years on a residence permit or right of residence. Study permit time does not count.
Passed the basic adaptation training.
Income at least the subsistence level, set yearly by the State Budget Act.
Health insurance required.
Special rules for doctoral degree holders and people who came as close relatives.

sources.label: Police and Border Guard Board: residence permit for a permanent resident

stay.note: Temporary permit up to 5 years, extensions up to 10 years at a time.

routes.name: EU/EEA/Swiss right of residence
routes.summary: Citizens of EU and EEA countries and Switzerland don't need a residence permit to live in Estonia. They register their right of residence instead.

other: Registration conditions not read.

sources.label: Police and Border Guard Board: residence permits

routes.name: Estonian citizenship by naturalization (adult)
routes.summary: Needs 8 years of residence, at least 5 of them on a permanent basis, plus language and constitution exams. Adults generally can't keep another citizenship.

eligibility.language: Estonian language exam (unless educated in Estonian)
other: 8 years of residence in Estonia, at least 5 as a permanent resident.
Hold a long-term residence permit or right of permanent residence.
Pass exam on the Constitution and the Citizenship Act.
Permanent legal income.
Registered address in the population register.
Loyalty to the Estonian state.
Dual citizenship rules are not on the cited page. Confirm with the Police and Border Guard Board.

citizenship.note: Dual citizenship not stated on the cited page.

sources.label: Police and Border Guard Board: citizenship for an adult

routes.name: Business residence permit for company shareholders
routes.summary: For people who own part of an Estonian company and have invested at least 65,000 EUR in it. Permit is up to 5 years.

investment.note: Invested in the company's Estonian activities.

other: Company registered in the Estonian Business Register.
Income of six times the yearly subsistence level.
Health insurance required.
Needs a business plan in Estonian or English with 2-year financial forecasts.

stay.note: Extensions up to 10 years at a time.

routes.processing: Decision within 90 days, then the card is issued within 30 days.

sources.label: Police and Border Guard Board: residence permit for business

routes.name: Business residence permit for large investors
routes.summary: Invest at least 1 million EUR in an Estonian company or a fund that invests mainly in Estonian companies. Permit is up to 5 years.

investment.note: Must be a permanent direct investment.

other: Income of six times the yearly subsistence level.
Health insurance required.

stay.note: Extensions up to 10 years at a time.

routes.processing: Decision within 90 days, then the card is issued within 30 days.
